text: Deep learning models can grade diabetic retinopathy from fundus photographs with high accuracy. However, they rarely show why an image is referred, which limits their acceptance in primary care. In this study, we propose a model that grades referral urgency from the lesions it detects, so that each decision is traceable to visible evidence.

text: Most screening models are trained only with image-level labels. As a result, they may learn shortcuts such as camera artefacts or image borders instead of the lesions that ophthalmologists use. Such shortcuts are difficult to detect during development and may fail when the model is deployed on images from a new camera.

text: LesionTriage outperformed all baselines on the external test set (Table 2). Compared with the image-level classifier, it improved sensitivity from 0.86 to 0.92 while keeping specificity above 0.90. Removing the lesion branch reduced AUC by 0.03, indicating that lesion evidence contributes to the referral decision.

text: This study has several limitations. First, all images were collected in one country, and the results may not hold for populations with different disease prevalence. Second, lesion annotations were available only for the development set. Future work will evaluate the system prospectively in community clinics.
